public_rationale: The condition concerns industry revenue by 2030 and is not established as of October 28, 2026. Under the conditional-forecast rule, the claim cannot yet be scored. Anthropic's risk disclosure supplies context but establishes neither the condition nor either predicted consequence.
limitations: This is a temporary conditional hold.
The investment-viability and company-payment consequences require separate evidence.
Payment obligations extending beyond 2030 need separate treatment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If AI revenue does not reach over $2 trillion a year by 2030, the data center capex will not make sense and neither Anthropic nor OpenAI will be able to pay their commitments.
conditions: if AI does not generate over $2 trillion in annual revenue by 2030

statement.excerpt: When I say that, I mean it absolutely has to do that otherwise none of the data center capex makes sense, and neither Anthropic nor OpenAI can pay their commitments.

from_speaker: it absolutely has to do that
otherwise none of the data center capex makes sense
neither Anthropic nor OpenAI can pay their commitments
over $2 trillion in annual revenue by 2030, from the preceding sentence
our_interpretation: The antecedent is failure of annual generative AI and AI compute revenue to exceed USD 2 trillion by December 31, 2030. Equality with USD 2 trillion does not satisfy 'over'.
The consequence has two parts: the referenced data-center investment is financially unjustified, and each named company is unable to pay its commitments.
I read 'none' and 'neither' literally. A demonstrably viable covered investment or either company's demonstrated ability to pay would challenge the corresponding part.
Ability to pay includes available cash, operating receipts, and financing. Losses alone do not establish inability to pay.
Only payments contractually due through the deadline are tested as due payments; multiyear commitment totals are not assumed immediately payable.
The commitment amounts in the surrounding discussion are estimates. The revenue antecedent is an industry-wide measure separate from the companies' payment obligations.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the revenue antecedent and shows that the referenced data-center investment is financially unjustified and that both Anthropic and OpenAI cannot meet the relevant payments when due.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With the revenue antecedent established, evidence shows that a covered data-center investment is financially viable or that either Anthropic or OpenAI can meet its relevant commitments. Assess the two consequences separately if evidence differs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Establish whether annual industry revenue fails to exceed USD 2 trillion by the deadline, then examine investment viability and each company's ability to pay the covered obligations. If the antecedent does not occur, the conditional forecast remains unscored.
